items.title: John Pizzarelli, Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: there’s Johnny Mandel, there’s Michel Legrand and his entire French orchestra who just came in off a plane to play a concert

ctx.x: This will only take 25 minutes. Talk about blessed, I mean everywhere along the way, something good happened. And so Chesky Records makes a record of Johnny Frigo and me and Bucky, Ron Carter or Michael Moore and Butch Miles playing with Johnny

Frigo, you know, a violin player. And we all sat around the mic and play acoustic jazz, and then Chesky, David and Norman Chesky, the had just started the label. They go like, “We’re looking for a male singer, you know any male singers who could be on—” I said “Why don’t you come hear my group?” So they’d come to the thing, they’d hear my trio up at Jay’s when it used to be a great club here in New York, and I finished the set and David Chesky says, “well we’re going to get Milt Hinton and Clark Terry and your…

okay. Aside from then having like personal troubles in my life, I’m like losing my voice, in between all of this stuff that’s going on. But the record gets made. And then we go to promote it, and Sebesky, we’re going to promote it at the Blue Note and Sebesky writes new chart for the band, and Ron Fair says, “well we’ve got to record Avalon, this is all new, we need to do that as well as” — well we were doing the Christmas in the middle of the show. We go in the studio and it’s January and we record all this,…
